description: FIND-202's fix precisely scopes the txHash-replay blocklist to 'the set of every txHash ALREADY recorded on a previously-verified, CREDITED repayment row' (lines 1104-1109) -- this correctly handles the manifest's specific question about an already-REJECTED row (a rejected/failed verification correctly does NOT count as 'already credited', so a transiently-rejected-then-later-legitimately-finalized real transaction is not wrongly permanently blacklisted). However, the SAME paragraph's Edge Cases introduce an undefined term that creates a NEW, unresolved ambiguity: a same-loan replay is 'rejected... LOGGED as a replay attempt' (line 1152-1154) and a cross-loan replay is 'rejected... identically (credit 0, LOGGED)' (line 1157-1159). Neither the EARS text, the Edge Cases, nor any Acceptance Criterion (nor any PROP in verification-architecture.md) ever specifies whether 'logged' means (a) an out-of-band audit/console log entirely OUTSIDE loans.jsonl (in which case this has zero interaction with any other computation), or (b) a NEW row APPENDED to loans.jsonl for the SAME loan_id (which the word choice 'logged as a replay attempt' -- as opposed to 'silently returns 0' -- suggests, given every OTHER event in this entire feature, without exception, is recorded via a loans.jsonl append per ledger.js's own generic readChildren/appendChild primitives, and this spec never introduces or names any OTHER logging mechanism anywhere). If (b) is the intended reading, this creates a genuine correctness risk this spec never reconciles: EVERY other reduction in this document (sumOutstandingPrincipalUsd, isBorrowerEligible's condition (c), countSuccessfulOnTimeRepayments, detectDefaultedLoans, computeColdStartRepaymentRate) treats 'the last-appended row for a given loan_id' as that loan's single authoritative current state (last-write-wins, explicitly established and relied upon throughout). If a rejected-replay-attempt row is ALSO appended to loans.jsonl for the SAME loan_id under attack, and its own shape does not exactly reproduce every field of that loan's actual current terminal state (status/repaid_usd/total_due_usd/on_time), it would become the new 'last row' and could silently corrupt every downstream computation for that loan_id (e.g. an attacker resubmitting an old, already-credited txHash against an ACTIVE loan could, merely by triggering a 'rejected, logged' append with an incomplete/different row shape, cause that loan's own repaid_usd/status to appear different to the NEXT read than its true, pre-replay-attempt value) -- exactly the class of hazard the last-write-wins convention exists to make unambiguous everywhere else in this spec. Separately, and reinforcing the same underlying gap: this feature never states a single, canonical loans.jsonl row-schema table (the full field set is only ever assembled piecemeal, one or two fields at a time, across REQ-101/104/106/108/109's own prose) and uses the SAME generic field name `txHash` for BOTH a loan's own disbursement transaction (recorded on REQ-106's 'active' follow-up row, lender->borrower) and a borrower's own repayment transaction(s) (recorded via REQ-108's verifyRepayment, borrower->lender) with no discriminator field (e.g. an explicit `event`/`kind` marker) ever specified to distinguish the two purposes structurally. PROP-108e's own binding proof obligation ('reads the FULL loans.jsonl ledger and rejects a txHash already recorded as credited anywhere in it') depends entirely on an implementer correctly excluding disbursement-side txHash values from this scan -- a distinction the schema itself never makes explicit or verifiable.

evidence.snippet: A caller resubmits a txHash that was already verified and credited toward THIS SAME loan_id's own repaid_usd: THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it (credit 0, logged as a replay attempt) ... A caller submits a txHash that was already verified and credited toward a DIFFERENT loan_id ... THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it identically (credit 0, logged).

crossCheck.note: PROP-108e's own test method never specifies the row/log shape a rejected replay produces, nor tests that a rejected-replay log entry (if appended to loans.jsonl) preserves the loan's own prior terminal state under the last-write-wins reduction every other PROP in this document relies on. No PROP anywhere in this 48-obligation document defines a canonical loans.jsonl row schema or a discriminator distinguishing a disbursement-event txHash from a repayment-event txHash.
